Text: Excellent. Thank you. Mayor, assistant mayor, members of the council,  I'm honored to present to you the Claremont Fire Department fiscal year 26 budget.  Before I enter the formal budget request, I would like to update you on some of the continued goals and objectives that we have been working on for the last fiscal year.  First and foremost, our top priority with the fire Department is to provide   for the safety and well-being of our community members.

Speaker: Speaker 20
Text: Last calendar year, the Claremont Fire Department responded to just under 1400 calls encompassing structure fires, brush fires, motor vehicle accidents, medical issues and just about any other type of incident that you can imagine.  Our members answered every call for service, including all of our 26 mutual aid requests.  Additionally, we have placed a strong emphasis on our Code Enforcement Division, which has worked extremely hard inspecting and enforcing and bringing our buildings up to code.

Speaker: Speaker 20
Text: Due to these efforts, we are now in a position to target buildings that, for lack of better words, have been left behind due to the backlog in code enforcement. It is important for the Council to note that my vision with code enforcement is built upon community risk reduction, and that is preventing the incident before it begins.  To illustrate this, I'd like you to imagine approaching the five way stop on Mulberry Street at 2 a.m. and for a split second you contemplate running that intersection.

Speaker: Speaker 20
Text: But as you approach, you see a police officer on the other side of that intersection, and it makes you come to a complete stop. That officer's presence alone mitigated that infarction. Where the fire department differs from our friends in blue is that we can't simply drive around in our apparatus and prevent overloaded electrical outlets,  improper chimney cleaning, and improper cooking practices.

Speaker: Speaker 20
Text: This highlights the importance of our fire prevention division  preventing incidents before they begin.  Last calendar year alone, our Code Enforcement Division handled nearly 650 inspections, including multifamily dwellings, places of assembly, oral burner permits, schools and more than two family dwellings, just to name a few.  Moving to the operational side of the house, we have made significant strides in recruitment and retention.

Speaker: Speaker 20
Text: Currently, the Claremont Fire Department is at full staff as we have successfully onboarded our newest member who returned from the Academy last December. We have also seen a huge increase in interest in our department and as a result of the high quality of candidates, we were able to establish a hiring list where we were able to rank the candidates based on their interview and oral board performance.

Speaker: Speaker 20
Text: That list is valid for one year and will be updated this August. Having this list in place will allow us to expedite the hiring process should we see any turnover.  Our operations deputy, who is sitting to my left in your right, has continued focusing on training efforts, successfully holding our first live burn training at our conics containers. He has also implemented joint trainings with our mutual aid partners, further strengthening our collaborations with our mutual aid friends.

Speaker: Speaker 20
Text: The department was successful in obtaining the Fire Prevention and Safety Grant, which allowed us to continue our smoke detector program. Speaker: Speaker 20
Text: One of our biggest accomplishments was a refurbishment of engine three. Thanks to our efforts and efforts to strengthen partnerships with local businesses, Ford of Claremont generously donated a new F150 vehicle to replace our aging car two.

Speaker: Speaker 20
Text: That vehicle came lettered and equipped with emergency lighting, saving taxpayers approximately $70,000. We have also made significant gains in maintaining our traffic light systems.
